model: IN485MHI001R000 (Mitsubishi Heavy Industries gateway, BACnet MS/TP)
equipment_type: VRF / split air conditioner BACnet gateway (1 indoor unit or group)
applies_to: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries residential and VRF indoor units on the X-Y wired remote-controller bus (one unit or a group that acts as one).
summary: BACnet MS/TP-only Intesis interface for one Mitsubishi Heavy Industries indoor unit, connected anywhere on the X-Y remote-controller bus. It exposes 35 fixed objects: on/off, mode, setpoint, fan and up/down vane as _command/_status pairs, error code, error and filter resets, occupancy logic, a remote lock, outdoor temperature, the Center/Remote control state and a virtual-temperature function.
notes: Sibling of the INBACMHI001R000 (BACnet IP and MS/TP), listed separately. This MS/TP model adds the virtual-temperature objects (AI 17, BI 14) and DIP switch read-backs.
The manual's object list gives ErrorAddress as AI 2, which clashes with ErrorCode; its property table says AI 4, used here.
Fan speed Auto (state 1) may be missing on older indoor units.
Object names follow each object's Object_Name property where it differs only in capitals (SetPoint_status, SetPoint_command, OccupiedCoolSetPoint and siblings, UnoccupiedDeadbandAction).
User_Setpoint_status has no property table in the manual; its units are not stated.
Temperature objects follow the °C/°F DIP switch setting.

source.title: IN485MHI001R000 Gateway - Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Residential and VRF Systems to BACnet MS/TP - User Manual

integration.summary: Connect the gateway anywhere on the X-Y bus (no polarity), set the MS/TP MAC address on SW2 and the bus role on SW1-1, then write the _command objects (on/off, mode, setpoint, fan) and read back the _status objects. Units grouped on one remote bus act as one.

minimum_points.name: SetPoint_status
minimum_points.why: Setpoint the unit is really using

integration.enable: No enable point is documented; the gateway accepts commands once it talks to the unit. MI 9 CenterRemote shows whether the BMS, the wired remote or both may control the unit; BV 2 LockRemoteControl locks the remote.
integration.remote_sensors: With the gateway as X-Y header (SW1-1 on), reading temperature from the remote (SW1-2 on) and the unit set to use the remote's sensor, the value written to AO 1 RoomTemperature_command becomes the unit's reference temperature; until a valid value is written the unit may show a thermistor error. Otherwise the Virtual Temperature function recalculates the setpoint from AO 1 (BI 14 shows it is active, AI 17 the BMS setpoint).
setup: Baud rate on SW1 P6-P8; autobaud is the default.
MS/TP MAC address on SW2 P1-P7; device instance 246000 + MAC unless Object_Identifier is written from BACnet (manual addressing until a factory reset).
SW1-1: follower on the X-Y bus (default) or header. With no wired remote installed, set the gateway as header.
Factory reset: all SW1 and SW2 switches ON, power-cycle, then all OFF within 30 seconds.
gotchas: If an MHI wired remote is on the bus, one of the two must be header and the other follower.
The Occupancy MV and its four setpoint AVs drive built-in logic; leave Occupancy at 3 (Disabled) if the BMS handles scheduling.
Write the _command object and read the _status object.
